track: Track G Escuelita alumni continuity and solidarity
source_file: public alumni statements and event notices linked in the unit source inventory
article_title: Escuelita alumni as continuing translocal collective actors
author: UNAM members and regional alumni and allies
community_group: Escuelita alumni across Mexico, Italy, and other locations
evidence_type: primary or participant-authored public movement records
exact_factual_observation: Within months of the first sessions, Escuelita alumni in several geographies publicly identified and acted together through denunciations, solidarity statements, fundraising, and coordination. Alumni remained a named constituency in Valley of Mexico action in 2015 and CompArte and CNI activity in 2016.
what_source_establishes: The Escuelita produced or reinforced an alumni relation that reached lineage level 2 and supported repeated collective action across multiple places for at least three years.
what_source_does_not_establish: It does not give the number or proportion of alumni active, prove continuous membership of any group, isolate the Escuelita from prior Sixth Declaration ties, or establish a new communal institution or human outcome.
author_interpretation: The records frame shared learning and solidarity as an obligation to act with threatened Zapatista and Indigenous communities.
alternative_interpretation: Many participants were already activists; the Escuelita may have intensified an existing network rather than created it. Public archives disproportionately preserve visible solidarity actions.
response_process: shared participant identity; local coordination; public statements; fundraising; marches; cultural and political events
outcome: Documented alumni mobilization from 2014 through 2016; organizational persistence and human outcomes are unmeasured.
transferability: High for distinguishing continued relation from inspiration. Medium for attributing network creation to the Escuelita. Low for communal replication.
likely_article_destination: Worldwide communal innovation / movement continuity / alumni infrastructure
notes: Lineage level 2. Do not count every Sixth Declaration action as an Escuelita outcome.

track: Track G Escuelita practice transfer and seed pedagogics
source_file: CIIS transcript and qualitative Zapatista seed-pedagogics studies
article_title: Participant follow-up and translocal Zapatista seed pedagogics
author: Charlotte Maria Saenz; Zara Zimbardo
page_locator: public transcript and publisher or repository abstracts
source_access: public transcript and indexed scholarly records inspected
evidence_type: first-person retrospective follow-up plus qualitative interview research
exact_factual_observation: A delegation organizer reported encountering former students later and seeing principles carried into care, organizing, political, and NGO work. Qualitative studies with pro-Zapatista interlocutors describe changes in listening, hierarchy, memory, and collective organization outside Chiapas.
what_source_establishes: There is credible lineage-level-3 evidence that Zapatista encounters, including the Escuelita, informed later practice and collectivities.
what_source_does_not_establish: The exposure combines the Escuelita with other encounters and long accompaniment. The sources do not identify an Escuelita-only cohort, name a denominator, count failures, or measure institutional durability and human outcomes.
author_interpretation: Saenz theorizes a life-long mutual political-ethical education rather than export of a fixed institutional recipe.
alternative_interpretation: Sympathetic participants may overreport transformation, and the observed effects may come from prior activism, later encounters, or selection into the delegations.
response_process: immersive learning; return to home contexts; reflection on hierarchy; practice adaptation; continuing encounter networks
outcome: Reported practice transfer and collective political learning; no comparative or longitudinal outcome panel.
transferability: Medium-high for recognizing practice transfer as a separate diffusion outcome. Low for causal effect size or successful community replication.
likely_article_destination: Worldwide communal innovation / internal school-research function / diffusion measurement
notes: Lineage level 3 with bundled exposure. Keep it separate from levels 4 through 6.

track: Track G Escuelita-linked durable coordination candidate
source_file: officially reposted 2016-2022 records and 2024 CNI statement
article_title: Espacio de Coordinacion Grietas en el Muro as a mixed-lineage sprout candidate
author: Grietas en el Muro and partner collectives
page_locator: complete public event and signatory records
evidence_type: organization event trail and movement-primary signatory records
exact_factual_observation: A 2016 CompArte notice says collectives and individuals including Sixth Declaration adherents and Escuelita students created an alternate festival site and names Espacio de Coordinacion Grietas en el Muro among organizers. The coordination space appears in 2019 and 2022 organizing records and as a named Mexican signatory in an October 2024 CNI statement.
what_source_establishes: This is the strongest located lineage-level-4 candidate: a named post-Escuelita coordination space created with an explicit alumni role and publicly visible over at least eight years.
what_source_does_not_establish: The founding record is explicitly mixed-lineage and does not assign sole causation to the Escuelita. The trail does not prove continuous membership, internal governance, residential communal life, practice fidelity, or human outcomes.
author_interpretation: The organizers present art, exchange, memory, travel, and solidarity as tools for building resistance and autonomy in their own context.
alternative_interpretation: The name may have consolidated preexisting collectives around one event, while later appearances could reflect a small or changing core. Public visibility is not institutional health.
response_process: local response to movement call; coordination space; repeated events; CNI solidarity; durable public identity
outcome: Public activity from 2016 through at least October 2024; no level-5 shared-life institution or level-6 outcome evidence.
transferability: High for a durable named coordination trail. Medium for Escuelita contribution to origin. Low for residential-governance replication.
likely_article_destination: Worldwide communal innovation / movement continuity / candidate descendant case
notes: Lineage level 4, mixed origin. This is a political-cultural coordination institution, not a replicated Zapatista municipality.

track: Track G named Escuelita participant pathway
source_file: Briarpatch participant account and later institutional-repository publication record
author: Levi Gahman
community_group: Okanagan Valley student organizers; RAMA; public and scholarly audiences
page_locator: complete 2014 article and indexed later records
evidence_type: named participant microhistory and public knowledge transmission
exact_factual_observation: A former Escuelita student documented a 2014 student solidarity mobilization, was identified as organizing with RAMA, later thanked the Zapatistas for accepting him into their school, and continued public and scholarly work on autonomy, mutual aid, food sovereignty, and social reproduction.
what_source_establishes: A named individual trace connects participation to later organizing and knowledge transmission, avoiding a wholly anonymous influence claim.
what_source_does_not_establish: It does not establish that the Escuelita created RAMA, caused the action, produced organizational adoption, or generated later communal or human outcomes. One individual cannot represent the cohort.
author_interpretation: Gahman presents Zapatismo as a practical source for anti-capitalist, decolonial, gender-just collective life.
alternative_interpretation: The participant was already aligned with the Sixth and may have entered the Escuelita through prior organizing; later work may reflect broader Zapatista engagement.
response_process: attendance; solidarity action; migrant-support organizing; writing and teaching
outcome: Observable continuing pathway; causal contribution and outcome are unmeasured.
transferability: Medium for a named lineage trace. Low for generalization or institutional replication.
likely_article_destination: Worldwide communal innovation / participant pathways / qualitative examples
notes: Lineage level 3 and possibly 4 only if a later project documents adoption; the current record does not.

source_file: pre-2013 scholarly records on transnational Zapatismo, Casa del Pueblo, and Universidad de la Tierra Califas
article_title: Transnational Zapatista diffusion predates the Escuelita
author: Abigail Andrews; Kara Zugman Dellacioppa; Manuel Callahan
community_group: Northern activist networks; Casa del Pueblo; Universidad de la Tierra Califas
page_locator: publisher abstracts, book description, and open indexed article summary
evidence_type: pre-event ethnography, movement research, and practice-grounded political theory
exact_factual_observation: Before the 2013 Escuelita, scholars documented activists taking Zapatismo home, Zapatista-inspired community organizations in Los Angeles and Mexico City, Casa del Pueblo organizing undocumented immigrants, and UT Califas as collective pedagogy and Zapatismo beyond Chiapas.
what_source_establishes: The Escuelita entered an existing transnational Zapatista ecology. A post-2013 date or Zapatista resemblance cannot establish Escuelita descent; explicit participant or organizational lineage is required.
what_source_does_not_establish: The controls do not show that the Escuelita had no later effect on these networks or that every later project was preexisting. They do not evaluate post-2013 reinforcement or grafting.
author_interpretation: The authors describe adaptation, reflexivity, and complex South-to-North networks rather than simple institutional copying.
alternative_interpretation: Later Escuelita participation could materially strengthen, redirect, or connect an older organization without being its founding cause.
response_process: date the organization; identify prior Zapatista exposure; require explicit lineage; classify reinforcement separately from creation
outcome: Strong pre-2013 evidence of broader Zapatista diffusion; no Escuelita-specific outcome by definition.
transferability: High for causal attribution control and for the grafting distinction.
likely_article_destination: Worldwide communal innovation / source-quality and lineage audit
notes: Preexisting soil is evidence of Zapatista success, but not an Escuelita seedling.

track: Track G Escuelita descendant bounded null
source_file: bounded public search across primary movement archives, alumni actions, scholarly studies, participant traces, candidate organizations, and pre-event controls
journal_volume_issue_year: records through October 2024 located in a search completed 2026-08-15
article_title: No located Escuelita descendant reaches durable communal replication plus measured human outcomes
author: research synthesis
community_group: Escuelita alumni and candidate descendant projects
page_locator: source inventory and report search lanes
source_access: bounded public search; no inaccessible or private alumni archive claimed
exact_factual_observation: The search located no public participant registry, longitudinal or comparative alumni cohort, counted adoption or failure rate, new residential community or autonomous governing federation with an explicit Escuelita founding chain, or later safety, child-wellbeing, autonomy, retention, material-viability, and relational outcomes.
what_source_establishes: The current evidence ceiling is lineage level 4 for one mixed-origin coordination space. Stronger claims of durable communal replication or success remain unverified.
what_source_does_not_establish: This does not establish historical absence. Quiet projects, failed attempts, renamed adaptations, nonpublic records, and nonindexed languages or geographies may be missing.
author_interpretation: not applicable; this is a bounded synthesis disposition
alternative_interpretation: The absence of systematic follow-up may reflect a movement ethic against standardized replication or surveillance as well as ordinary archival loss.
response_process: define lineage ladder; search named alumni and projects; apply pre-event controls; record the evidence ceiling and missing denominator
outcome: No level-5 direct descendant or level-6 outcome panel located; levels 2-4 have positive evidence.
transferability: High for defining the missing evidence and preventing overclaiming. Medium for the bounded null because the search cannot cover private and unnamed adaptations.
likely_article_destination: Worldwide communal innovation / outcome dashboard / research agenda
notes: A bounded null is a result about this search, not proof that no Escuelita descendant exists.
